description: Planted leaks in demo/broken. Each leak lists the check ids that must report "leak" on demo/broken and "pass" on demo/fixed, and the schema warnings it must raise on demo/broken. The integration tests compare these lists exactly: no leak may be missed and no extra leak may appear. All data in the demo is synthetic.

leaks.description: Row level security was never switched on, so every client, signed in or not, can read and change every organisation's contacts.
leaks.fix: Enable row level security and add a membership policy.

warnings.object: public.contacts

leaks.category: Policies written but row level security not enabled (missing protection)
leaks.description: The expense policy is correct, but row level security is not enabled on the table, so Postgres ignores the policy.
leaks.fix: Enable row level security on the table.

warnings.object: public.expenses
public.expenses

leaks.description: The read policy is USING (true), so any signed-in user reads every organisation's projects.
leaks.fix: Limit the read policy to the user's own organisations.

warnings.object: policy "Signed-in users read projects" on public.projects

leaks.description: The read policy checks that the user belongs to some organisation, not to the invoice's organisation.
leaks.fix: Compare the invoice's org_id with the user's memberships.

warnings.object: policy "Members read invoices" on public.invoices

leaks.description: The insert policy only checks that the user is signed in, so a user can create projects inside another organisation.
leaks.fix: Give the insert policy a WITH CHECK on the user's own organisations.

warnings.object: policy "Signed-in users create projects" on public.projects

leaks.description: The update policy only checks that the user is signed in. With no WITH CHECK, Postgres reuses that rule for the new row, so a user can also move their own invoice into another organisation.
leaks.fix: Limit USING and WITH CHECK to the user's own organisations.

warnings.object: policy "Signed-in users update invoices" on public.invoices
policy "Signed-in users update invoices" on public.invoices

leaks.category: Re-assigning a row to another tenant (WITH CHECK (true))
leaks.description: The update policy checks the project before the change, but WITH CHECK (true) accepts any new org_id, so a member can hand a project to another organisation.
leaks.fix: Use the same membership rule in WITH CHECK as in USING.

warnings.object: policy "Members update their projects" on public.projects

leaks.description: The read and delete policies on tasks are USING (true). Postgres only deletes rows the user can also see, so both are open and any signed-in user can see and delete every organisation's tasks.
leaks.fix: Reach tasks through their project, whose own policy checks membership.

warnings.object: policy "Signed-in users read tasks" on public.tasks
policy "Signed-in users delete tasks" on public.tasks

leaks.description: Profiles, including phone numbers, are readable by anyone, even visitors who are not signed in.
leaks.fix: Limit profiles to their own user, for signed-in users only.

warnings.object: policy "Profiles are public" on public.profiles

leaks.description: Visitors who are not signed in can file quote requests into any organisation.
leaks.fix: Accept quote requests only from members (or from a server route using the service role).

warnings.object: policy "Visitors submit quote requests" on public.quote_requests

leaks.description: The receipts bucket is public, so anyone with a link can download every user's receipts.
leaks.fix: Make the bucket private and serve files through signed URLs.

warnings.object: receipts

leaks.category: Storage read policy ignores the folder
leaks.description: The documents read policy only checks the bucket, so any signed-in user can list and download every organisation's documents.
leaks.fix: Check that the first folder of the path is one of the user's organisations.

leaks.category: Storage write policies ignore the folder
leaks.description: The documents upload, replace and delete policies only check the bucket, so any signed-in user can add, replace and delete files in other organisations' folders.
leaks.fix: Check the organisation folder in every write policy.

leaks.category: SECURITY DEFINER function reads another tenant's data
leaks.description: The function runs as its owner, which skips row level security, and never checks membership, so anyone can read any organisation's invoices by passing its id.
leaks.fix: Make the function SECURITY INVOKER (and stop anonymous visitors from calling it).

warnings.object: public.get_org_invoices(p_org_id uuid)

leaks.category: SECURITY DEFINER function deletes another tenant's data
leaks.description: The same mistake in a function that deletes: anyone can delete any organisation's project (and its tasks).
leaks.fix: Make the function SECURITY INVOKER so the projects delete policy applies.

warnings.object: public.delete_project(p_project_id uuid)

leaks.category: View that bypasses row level security
leaks.description: The view has no security_invoker, so it runs with its owner's rights and shows every organisation's clients to every caller.
leaks.fix: Create the view WITH (security_invoker = true) and revoke anonymous access.

warnings.object: public.client_directory

leaks.description: Materialized views cannot have row level security, and this one is readable by every client, so every organisation's revenue is visible.
leaks.fix: Revoke client access to the materialized view.

warnings.object: public.org_revenue

leaks.category: Child table owned only through its parent
leaks.description: Payments have no organisation column; they belong to an organisation through their invoice. The read policy ignores that and is USING (true).
leaks.fix: Reach payments through their invoice, whose own policy checks membership.

warnings.object: policy "Signed-in users read payments" on public.payments

leaks.category: Shared table that clients can write
leaks.description: Plans are reference data every organisation relies on, but any signed-in user can add, change or delete them.
leaks.fix: Keep only the public read policy; changes go through the service role.

warnings.object: policy "Signed-in users add plans" on public.plans
policy "Signed-in users change plans" on public.plans
policy "Signed-in users delete plans" on public.plans
